confirm.archive_remove: Take {what} out of {archive}? The archive is written anew without it; there is no trash inside an archive.
confirm.no_trash_here: No trash on this disk: delete {what} for good?
disk_image.unknown: Its format was not recognized from its header; 7-Zip may still read it.
dupes.before_scan: Pick the folders to compare, then Scan. Nothing goes to the trash without asking.

dupes.confirm_text.one: Move {n} copy ({size}) to the trash? At least one copy of each stays.
dupes.confirm_text.other: Move {n} copies ({size}) to the trash? At least one copy of each stays.

dupes.mark_tip: Mark to move to the trash
error.trash: Could not move {what} to the trash

error.counted_trash.one: {done} of {all} moved to the trash; {n} could not be moved to the trash
error.counted_trash.other: {done} of {all} moved to the trash; {n} could not be moved to the trash

feature.delete.a2: Not every file system has a trash the system can use. The error names the file. Use {delete_forever} to delete it for good, after checking.
feature.delete.q2: Moving to the trash fails on a network share or a USB stick.
feature.delete.what: {delete} moves the marked files to the system's trash; {delete_forever} deletes them for good. Both ask first.
feature.duplicates.a2: They go to the trash, not away for good, and at least one copy of each group always stays. Check with Show first if the folder matters.
feature.duplicates.what: In the desktop app, {duplicates} finds duplicate files and folders by content and moves extra copies to the trash.
feature.move_and_rename.q2: I moved files into a zip. Are the originals in the trash?
feature.undo.a1: A move to the trash, yes, except on a Mac and in the Flatpak, where you restore it from the system's trash. Deleting for good ({delete_forever}) cannot be undone.
feature.undo.a3: No. The history lives in memory, for the app run. After a restart, a move to the trash can still be restored from the system's trash.
feature.undo.what: {undo} undoes the last file operation (copy, move, rename, new folder, trash, pack, extract, permissions and dates), up to 20 back.

stop.done.trash.one: Stopped: {n} of {all} moved to the trash
stop.done.trash.other: Stopped: {n} of {all} moved to the trash

termux.no_trash_storage: No trash on the phone's storage: delete {what} for good?
undo.no_restore: the trash here gives nothing back to apps: restore it from the system's trash
undo.no_restore_hint: {key} cannot bring it back here: restore it from the system's trash
undo.no_trash: cannot go to the trash from here, so it is left as it is
sync.delete: Also delete what is only in {dir} (to the trash)
sync.about: Plan first: every copy, replacement and deletion is listed before anything changes. What is replaced or deleted goes to the trash; {undo} undoes it all.
sync.planned: {n} steps: {copies} to copy, {replaces} to replace, {deletes} to the trash ({size} to copy)
sync.kept: The trash could not take what was replaced or deleted: it is in {path}
feature.compare_folders.a2: From its menu: Make right like left or Make left like right plans every copy, replacement and deletion first, sends what it replaces or deletes to the trash, and {undo} undoes it. Or mark the differences and press {copy}. On Windows, and on a disk the trash could only copy to, it stays in a .coxswain-sync-… folder at the target's top instead. If the app was closed during a run, its next start sends that folder to the trash and says so; where the trash cannot take it, Disk use in Settings lists it with Remove.
sync.moved_away: The folder holding what was replaced or deleted was moved during the run, so it is not in the trash: {path}
notice.sync_binned: A folder sync that ended before it was finished had set aside {n} files ({size}) it replaced or deleted in {folder}. They are in the trash now, where you can restore them; {undo} no longer undoes that sync.
notice.sync_kept: A folder sync that has ended set aside {n} files ({size}) it replaced or deleted, and the trash cannot take them here, so they are still in {path}. {undo} no longer undoes that sync. Remove them in Settings → Privacy and updates → Disk use once you no longer need them.
disk.sync.what: {n} files a folder sync replaced or deleted in {folder}, kept here because the trash could not take them.
hint.blame: {key} shows who changed each line · {history} a function's history, in the viewer or the editor
viewer.keys_git: {blame} who changed each line · {history} history of this function
viewer.keys_history: ↑↓ PgUp PgDn move · / search · n N next, back · Esc back to the file
blame.too_long: git took too long: stopped after a minute
blame.not_here: Who changed each line is for files in a git, Jujutsu or Mercurial repository
blame.too_big: This file is too big to blame (over 32 MB)
blame.more_changes: Older changes left out: only the newest {n} are shown
blame.not_committed_file: This file is not in the last commit: it has no history yet
blame.not_in_head: {name} is not in the last commit: it has no history yet
blame.off: Who changed each line put away
blame.cut: Who changed each line: the first {n} lines
blame.shown: Who changed each line: commit, author and date before each line
blame.edited: The lines changed: save, then ask who changed them again
blame.save_first: Save first: who changed each line is of the file as saved
blame.history_where: A function's history: open the file ({view} or {edit}), put the cursor in the function, then {key}
blame.history_where_gui: A function's history: open the file in the editor ({edit}), put the cursor in the function, then {key}; or click a line's commit in the preview's Who changed
blame.tip: Commit, author and date before each line ({key})
blame.click_hint: Click a line's commit for the history of its function
blame.history_tip: The commits that changed the function the cursor is in, or the lines selected
blame.cut_gui: Only the start of the file is shown
feature.git_blame.title: Who changed each line
feature.git_blame.what: {blame} shows before each line of a file the commit that last changed it, its author and its date: in the viewer, the editor and the desktop app's preview.
feature.git_blame.q1: Why does a line say not committed yet?
feature.git_blame.a1: You changed or added it since the last commit. Once you commit, the line shows that commit.
feature.git_blame.q2: Why is nothing shown in the editor?
feature.git_blame.a2: It is of the file as saved: save first, then {blame}. Typing puts it away, since the lines move.
feature.git_blame.a3: Yes, through hg annotate with hg 5.4 or later: commit, author and date per line. Subversion and CVS are not asked.
feature.git_line_history.title: History of a function
feature.git_line_history.what: {line_history} lists the commits that changed the function the cursor is in, or the lines selected, each with its change.
feature.git_line_history.a1: The innermost named item at the cursor, found again by its name in the last commit. Select lines to follow those instead.
feature.git_line_history.q2: Why does it say the function is not in the last commit?
feature.git_line_history.a2: It is new or renamed since then, so it has no history yet. Commit it first.
feature.git_line_history.q3: Where do I ask it in the desktop app's preview?
feature.git_line_history.a3: Turn on Who changed at the top of the preview, then click a line's commit.
setting.search_commit_changes.hint: Off by default. Also searches what each commit changed: its diff, up to 64 KB a commit and 64 MB a repository. It can make search.db much larger; the size and time are said before it starts.
setting.search_commit_changes_in: Changes of commits, for these folders' repositories
setting.search_commit_changes_in.hint: With the option above off: keep the changes of the repositories in these folders alone.
changes.cost: Reading the changes of {commits} commits in {repos} repositories adds about {size} to search.db and takes about {secs} s in the background. Nothing leaves the machine.
changes.off: The changes of the commits of {repos} repositories are taken out of search.db, and the room is given back.
changes.cost_unknown: The changes of commits are read at the next scan of the repositories; Disk use then shows their size.
changes.costing: Working out what the changes of commits cost…
changes.freed: Changes of commits taken out at {at}: {size} freed
disk.changes.name: search.db: changes of commits
disk.changes.what: The text of what each commit changed, inside search.db (Settings → Finding files → Text of each commit's changes).
disk.changes.cost: Turns that option off: the text goes when the search helper next starts, and search.db gives the room back. Commit messages stay.
feature.search_history.what: Find searches the commit messages, authors, changed paths and changed functions of your git, Mercurial and Jujutsu repositories, under History; the text of the changes too, when turned on.
feature.search_history.a2: It keeps the names of the functions each commit changed, not the code. Turn on Text of each commit's changes in Settings to search the changes themselves.
setting.search_history.hint: Commit messages, authors, changed paths and changed functions of the git, Mercurial and Jujutsu repositories in the folders read.
action.bin_delete: Delete from the trash for good
sidebar.bin_tip: Opens the trash as a panel; right-click to empty it
bin.ask_empty: Empty the trash: delete {what} ({size}) for good? This cannot be undone.
bin.failed: Not everything in the trash could be done
bin.busy: Another Coxswain is working in the trash. Try again when it has finished.
bin.no_restore: macOS gives apps no way to put files back from the trash: copy them out, or use Put Back in Finder
bin.not_here: This works only in the trash
bin.read_only: Nothing is moved, renamed or made in the trash: restore it, or copy it out
bin.in_finder: The trash opened in Finder: Coxswain needs Full Disk Access to list it
bin.inside_tip: The system's trash: each file where it is in the trash, with the folder it came from and when it was deleted
notice.bin_mac: macOS: Coxswain lists the trash only with Full Disk Access (System Settings → Privacy & Security → Full Disk Access); without it the trash opens in Finder. Files cannot be put back from Coxswain, only deleted for good.
notice.bin_flatpak: In the Flatpak, Coxswain sees only its own trash, not the system's: what other apps, and Coxswain's Delete, put in the trash is not listed there.
hint.bin: {key}: restore what is under the cursor, delete it for good, or empty the trash
feature.bin.title: The trash
feature.bin.what: {bin} shows the system's trash as a panel, each file with the folder it came from and when it was deleted. {bin_restore} puts files back; {bin_delete} and {bin_empty} delete for good.
feature.bin.a1: Open the trash from the sidebar (in the terminal app from {goto_left}) or with {bin}, mark the file and use {bin_restore}. It goes back to the folder it came from, made again if it is gone.
feature.bin.a2: Nothing is overwritten. Coxswain asks, and restores it beside the other under a free name such as “report (2).pdf”, or leaves it in the trash.
feature.bin.a3: macOS gives apps no way to put a file back. With Full Disk Access Coxswain lists the trash and deletes for good; use Put Back in Finder to restore.
bin.finder_all_disks: Finder empties the trash of every disk, not only the one listed here.
